title: Amazon Blocks Meta's Muse: The Agentic Commerce War Splits Into Two Camps
desc: Amazon cut off Meta's Muse agent on September 20, then opened its seller tools to Claude. Shopify wired Shop Pay into Muse. What the two-camp split means for
keywords: amazon blocks meta muse, amazon muse ai agent blocked, agentic commerce war, meta muse shopify shop pay, amazon perplexity ninth circuit, ai shopping agents merchants, agentic checkout 2026
cta: Want your store reachable by the agents that will shop for your customers?
body:
September 25, 2026. In four days the largest players in online retail drew the map of agentic commerce. On Sunday September 20 Amazon cut off Meta's new Muse personal agent from shopping on Amazon.com, telling users that continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates its Conditions of Use, according to GeekWire. On Monday Shopify and Meta announced that Shop Pay would power checkout inside Muse. On Wednesday Amazon opened its own seller tools to outside agents, starting with Anthropic's Claude. For any e-commerce brand or agency, the message is that agents are coming to buy from you, but which agents, through which doors, is being decided platform by platform, and the store owner is not in the room.

What happened, in order

  1. September 8: Meta launched Muse, a personal agent that runs in a secure virtual machine with its own browser, connects to a user's services with credentials the user provides, and, where a site has no API, uses it through a browser the way a person would. Within a week it was the number one free app in Apple's U.S. App Store.
  2. September 20: Amazon blocked Muse. Its stated reasons: Meta did not tell Amazon the agent would access its store, the agent does not identify itself when it browses, and it appears to capture and store customer credentials. Amazon said it had asked Meta to exclude Amazon voluntarily and that talks were ongoing.
  3. September 21: Shopify and Meta said Shop Pay would power purchases inside Muse, adding to Stripe's Link, which already issues one-time-use cards for the agent. At Meta's Connect event on September 23, chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically, and named Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart and Wayfair as retail partners, per TechCrunch.
  4. September 23: Amazon announced a selling partner plugin that lets sellers run their stores from Claude and Amazon Quick, covered in our Seller Assistant plugin brief. Sellers' agents get in; shoppers' agents from rivals do not.
  5. The legal backdrop: Amazon won a preliminary injunction against Perplexity's Comet browser in March, lost it on August 4 when the Ninth Circuit ruled that the user, not the AI company, is the one accessing Amazon's computers under federal anti-hacking law, and was denied rehearing on September 10. The Muse block therefore cites contract terms, not hacking.

Why Amazon is fighting

GeekWire puts the stake at more than $68 billion of advertising revenue last year, a business that depends on people browsing Amazon's pages and seeing sponsored products. An agent that fetches the cheapest matching item and checks out never sees an ad. Amazon's own agent, Buy for Me, shops on external brands' sites, but the company points out it identifies itself and lets brands opt out, which is exactly the standard it is demanding of Meta. Amazon's counter-example is telling: food delivery apps and online travel agencies buy on customers' behalf every day, with the merchant's agreement. That is the model it wants for agents, and it is now the model it offers sellers through the Claude plugin.

What it means for operators

Two camps are forming. The open camp, Shopify, Stripe, Meta and the named retailers, wants agents to reach every catalog and complete checkout, with the platform taking the payment. The gated camp, Amazon, wants agents identified, agreed and, where possible, its own. A merchant on Shopify is now reachable by Muse whether or not they planned for it, so the product data, pricing rules and return policy an agent reads need to be right today, not after the first surprise order. A seller on Amazon should expect the reverse: outside shopping agents kept out, while Amazon hands them an agent of their own to run the back office. Either way, the reviews and ratings an agent reads to choose between two listings become the whole storefront, which is why review monitoring is the first thing we tighten for clients on both platforms, and why a service like Shopify app review management stops being a nice-to-have when the buyer is a machine that ranks by stars. Agencies should read the terms of every marketplace a client sells on for an agent clause this quarter; the Amazon language already exists, and the rest will follow.
faqs: Why did Amazon block Meta's Muse agent?

Amazon says Meta did not tell it Muse would access its store, that the agent does not identify itself when browsing, and that it appears to capture and store customer credentials. Amazon asked Meta to exclude Amazon voluntarily, then blocked the agent on September 20 citing its Conditions of Use.
Can Muse still shop on Shopify stores?

Yes. Shopify and Meta announced on September 21 that Shop Pay powers checkout inside Muse, and at Connect on September 23 Meta said Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically, alongside Stripe's Link one-time-use cards.
What did the Ninth Circuit rule in Amazon vs Perplexity?

On August 4, 2026 the Ninth Circuit lifted Amazon's preliminary injunction against Perplexity, ruling that the user, not the AI company, is the party accessing Amazon's computers under federal anti-hacking law. Amazon's petition for rehearing was denied on September 10, leaving contract and terms-of-service claims as its avenue.
What should merchants do about AI shopping agents?

Assume agents already read your catalog: make product data, pricing and return policies machine-accurate, monitor reviews and ratings closely because agents rank by them, and check each marketplace's terms for agent clauses. On Amazon, expect outside shopping agents to be blocked while Amazon's own seller agent tools expand.
